name: Agreement of June 23, 1874 by which the Eastern Shawnee sold part of their reserve for the Modocs (Royce area 571)
citation: Agreement of June 23, 1874, confirmed by Act of March 3, 1875, 18 Stat. 447 (Royce pp. 876-879)
promises: Not a treaty: by agreement of June 23, 1874 the Eastern Shawnee ceded a tract in the northeast corner of their reserve, about 4,000 acres, for the Modocs to occupy (Royce).
The tract ran south 2.5 miles along the Missouri state line from the reserve's northeast corner, west 2.5 miles, then north to the reserve line (Royce).
Congress confirmed the sale by Act of March 3, 1875, 18 Stat. 447 (Royce).
landTaken: Royce gives the tract as 4,000 acres, more or less, sold to the United States for the Modocs.
today: The Modoc Nation says the 4,000 acres were purchased for its people from the Eastern Shawnee in June 1874, after 153 Modoc prisoners of the Modoc War arrived at the Quapaw Agency in November 1873. No Indian Claims Commission finding about this sale was found.
openQuestions: The Eastern Shawnee Tribe's own history pages (estoo-nsn.gov) would not load for a robot (Cloudflare challenge, then 403); its account of the sale, said in search snippets to name a $6,000 price, was not read and is not recorded.
The price paid was not read in a primary source; Royce gives no figure. Whether it was fair was not examined by any decision found.
Indian Claims Commission Eastern Shawnee titles (Dockets 334-A, 13-G and related, 64) were listed; none concerns this 1874 sale. Docket 64 (compromise, 1977) was not read in full.
treaties.json links no statute for this record; Royce cites 18 Stat. 447 for the confirming Act.
Duplicate: the confirming Act is recorded under cession-1875-03-03-eastern-shawnee; same land (area 571), same event.

Audit 2026-11-08 (round 13): confirmed against the Royce pp. 876-878 page scans (Royce p. 877: "See act of Mar. 3, 1875, ratifying this agreement", area 571; p. 878: Stat. L. XVIII, 447, Modok). Wording "taking land by force" removed from the first promise: no source says so. ICC full-text searches (Eastern Shawnee Modoc; Shawnee Modocs 1874; Modoc Quapaw agency) found nothing on this sale; Docket 64 compromise findings (ICC id 2329) concern other cessions. Court of Claims case names (us-ct-cl vols 1-231) list no Eastern Shawnee or Modoc claim about it.
